**Synopsis:**
US Treasury Secretary Bessent met BOJ Governor Ueda at the G20 in Asheville, publicly endorsing decisive BOJ monetary tightening to address yen undervaluation and anchor inflation. Bessent's explicit backing effectively pre-commits the BOJ to a rate hike at its Sept 17-18 meeting. A joint US-Japan yen intervention on July 31 provided only temporary support. Markets are now near-fully pricing a September BOJ hike (following June's hike to 1%, a 31-year high), with analysts flagging possible quarterly hike cadence going forward.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — Indirectly but materially. Bessent's explicit endorsement of BOJ tightening signals US tolerance (even preference) for a stronger yen/weaker dollar dynamic. A BOJ hike accelerates JPY carry-trade unwind risk, historically a source of volatility for US equities and risk assets. It also reflects US comfort with current Fed policy independence — no signal of US rate changes embedded here.

However, Bessent's comfort pushing BOJ hawkishness without referencing Fed easing suggests the US side is not in a rush to cut; marginally tilts neutral-to-hawkish on implicit US rate framing. No new US rate catalyst embedded.
